raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm without aiter (`SGLANG_USE_AITER` unset, which is the normal setup on RDNA) and with vLLM installed, `layernorm.py` binds `fused_add_rms_norm` from `vllm._custom_ops`. vLLM's signature is the four-argument in-place one:

```
fused_add_rms_norm(input, residual, weight, epsilon) -> None
```

But `RMSNorm.forward_hip` and `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` call it with the six-argument out-of-place form. So the first forward with a residual, i.e. the second decoder layer of every model, fails:

```
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
```

This is not RDNA-specific. CDNA with aiter turned off hits it too. I reproduced it on gfx950 with vLLM 0.30, and on gfx1100 with vLLM 0.16 and 0.31. Part of the RDNA plan in #46900; the same fix applies to `main`.

## Modifications

- `RMSNorm.forward_hip` and `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` (vLLM branch):
  - Call `fused_add_rms_norm(x, residual, weight, eps)` in place and return `(x, residual)`, as `forward_cuda` already does with sgl-kernel's in-place kernel.
  - `residual` is made contiguous first, since vLLM's kernel requires it.
- Empty batches go to `forward_native`. The vLLM kernels fail to launch with an empty grid (`hipErrorInvalidConfiguration`), which I also hit on gfx1100.
- The aiter branches are unchanged.

**Regression test:** `test/registered/unit/layers/test_layernorm_hip_vllm.py` (CPU suite).
- It patches in a reference with vLLM's exact signature and in-place semantics, and checks `forward_hip` against `forward_native` for both classes, including an empty batch and `post_residual_addition`.
- It fails on the current code (`5 failed`, all `TypeError`) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

**Real vLLM kernel, gfx1100.** Radeon PRO W7900D, vLLM 0.31.0, torch 2.13, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`. Each case compares `forward_hip` to `forward_native` (fp32 reference math) for `(out, residual)`:

| case | `amd_march` | this PR: max abs err (out / residual) |
|---|---|---|
| RMSNorm bf16 [33, 4096] | TypeError | 3.1e-2 / 0 (1 bf16 ulp) |
| RMSNorm fp16 [33, 4096] | TypeError | 3.9e-3 / 0 |
| RMSNorm bf16 [2, 17, 4096] | TypeError | 3.1e-2 / 0 |
| RMSNorm bf16, non-contiguous residual | TypeError | 3.1e-2 / 0 |
| RMSNorm bf16, `post_residual_addition` | TypeError | 3.1e-2 / 6.3e-2 (summation order, same as `forward_cuda`) |
| RMSNorm empty batch | TypeError | OK |
| GemmaRMSNorm, same six cases | TypeError | same as RMSNorm, residual exact |

The same fix on `main`, checked on gfx950 (MI355X, vLLM 0.30.0, aiter off), gives the same numbers.

**Unit test** (CPU):

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `amd_march` | 5 failed, 2 passed |
| this PR | 2 passed (5 subtests) |

**End to end, gfx1100.** Qwen/Qwen3-8B bf16, TP1, default args (Triton attention, decode CUDA graph), vLLM 0.31 installed, no aiter. Applied on top of #46914, which makes the quark imports work without aiter. `sgl-eval==0.1.2` gsm8k, 200 examples, `enable_thinking=false`, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8: **0.955**. Without this change the scheduler dies on the first request with the `TypeError` above.

gfx1201 (R9700): the vLLM build I have for gfx1201 doesn't register the `_C` RMSNorm ops at all (`'_OpNamespace' '_C' object has no attribute 'rms_norm'`), so this path can't be exercised there. The CPU unit test covers the call shape, and the gfx1201 end-to-end run in #46914 uses `forward_native`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. The previous code could not run. The in-place call also drops the two `empty_like` allocations.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No doc change needed.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. (See above.)

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+"""On ROCm without aiter, RMSNorm and GemmaRMSNorm with a residual must call vLLM's
+fused_add_rms_norm with its in-place (input, residual, weight, epsilon) signature
+and match forward_native."""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers import layernorm
+from sglang.srt.layers.layernorm import GemmaRMSNorm, RMSNorm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+HIDDEN = 64
+
+
+def _vllm_fused_add_rms_norm(
+    input: torch.Tensor, residual: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, epsilon: float
+) -> None:
+    # Reference for vllm._custom_ops.fused_add_rms_norm: residual += input, then
+    # input = rms_norm(residual) * weight, both in place.
+    residual.add_(input)
+    r = residual.float()
+    normed = r * torch.rsqrt(r.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + epsilon)
+    input.copy_((normed * weight.float()).to(input.dtype))
+
+
+def _vllm_rms_norm(
+    out: torch.Tensor, input: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, epsilon: float
+) -> None:
+    x = input.float()
+    normed = x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + epsilon)
+    out.copy_((normed * weight.float()).to(out.dtype))
+
+
+class TestLayerNormHipVllm(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.patches = [
+            patch.object(layernorm, "_use_aiter", False),
+            patch.object(layernorm, "_has_vllm_rms_norm", True),
+            patch.object(
+                layernorm, "fused_add_rms_norm", _vllm_fused_add_rms_norm, create=True
+            ),
+            patch.object(layernorm, "rms_norm", _vllm_rms_norm, create=True),
+        ]
+        for p in self.patches:
+            p.start()
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        for p in reversed(self.patches):
+            p.stop()
+
+    def _check(self, layer, num_tokens, post):
+        x = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN)
+        residual = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN)
+        post_add = torch.randn(num_tokens, HIDDEN) if post else None
+        ref_out, ref_residual = layer.forward_native(
+            x.clone(), residual.clone(), None if post_add is None else post_add.clone()
+        )
+        out, out_residual = layer.forward_hip(x.clone(), residual.clone(), post_add)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref_out)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_residual, ref_residual)
+
+    def test_rms_norm_with_residual(self):
+        layer = RMSNorm(HIDDEN, eps=1e-6)
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            layer.weight.normal_(mean=1.0, std=0.1)
+        for num_tokens in (0, 7):
+            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens):
+                self._check(layer, num_tokens=num_tokens, post=False)
+
+    def test_gemma_rms_norm_with_residual(self):
+        layer = GemmaRMSNorm(HIDDEN, eps=1e-6)
+        layer.weight.weight_loader(layer.weight, torch.randn(HIDDEN) * 0.1)
+        for num_tokens, post in ((0, False), (7, False), (7, True)):
+            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens, post=post):
+                self._check(layer, num_tokens=num_tokens, post=post)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
